description: Experimental (the owner, 2026-11-06): Foxconn T99W640 / Dell DW5934e (Snapdragon X72) over USB, its MBIM composition 05c6:90d5 with cdc_mbim on interface 02 (dw5934e-5g-toolkit: USB\VID_05C6&PID_90D5&MI_02; 4PDA 1125602, kniga043 20.10.26: DIAG + ADB + MBIM). On USB it runs stably only when it powered up with PCIe connected and the PCIe bus was then cut physically (4PDA 1125602, Kilm 05.11.26); with PCIe left on it falls to no network until a reboot. The module is made for PCIe M.2 (MHI 105b:e11d eSIM, 105b:e11e, 105b:e118) and needs an M.2-to-USB adapter (4PDA 1125602, its first post: not USB out of the box). The ID is shared with the T99W175 in MBIM and the Compal RXM-G1: this profile takes it only by ModemManager's model (DMS over MBIM gives DP25-42843-47; a generic MBIM name leaves it to the T99W175 profile). Known faults, none curable from the router: a false PA temperature (sdr0_pa 131-137 °C at 34 °C) trips the modem's own thermal protection, which deregisters it and puts the radio to power save (powered, registration idle, no signal; persists across cold boots, a firmware fault: the toolkit's OEM fix request); a deadlock after a foreign base station's reject, held off by a periodic ping (4PDA 1125602 #59; the engine's reach checks send traffic anyway). So ModemManager alone, no AT, no driver rebind or USB re-authorize (a runtime driver switch killed the device in the toolkit's notes), recovery only on the operator's request, a long settle for the X72's boot. Reference: docs/modem-zoo/modems/foxconn-t99w640.md, observations F32, F33

recovery.source: experimental: reconnect, radio and reset through ModemManager on the operator's request only; no rebind or re-authorize (toolkit: a runtime driver switch gave «Device died»); the thermal fault is not cured by any reset
